ELI5: Why do healing cuts itch?

Two major causes: the actual act of multiplying cells and moving them to seal the gap in the skin causes pressure on the nerves that trigger an itch reflex, and chemicals released by the body during the healing process (histamine mostly) can irritate the skin slightly and cause the reflex. There can be other reasons, but those two are it most of the time.
So would taking an antihistamine, like benadryl, slow the healing of cuts on the body?

I don't think so. It might technically, but the histamine doesn't actually do much for the wound itself. It's released into a cut as a response to the open-air exposure and is meant to help protect from possible contaminants. So it probably wouldn't make it heal slower, but it would make you more susceptible to infection. This is all theoretically speaking, of course, and I'm not sure if it would actually have any real, noticeable effect.

Histamine (released from basophils and other granulocytes, not the neurotransmitters or the ones in the gut) increase tissue permeability to allow white blood cells to travel through/between the tight spaces of your cells to get to the site of injury or infection.
